input: Apply for a travel rewards credit card

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the user wants help narrowing down card options, completing the actual application, or both determines how far the plan needs to go.
Whether the card is for solo travel, a couple, a family, or a small business changes which rewards structures and supplementary card features matter most.
Different travelers prioritize different rewards — airline miles with a specific carrier, flexible transferable points, or hotel loyalty points — which narrows the card shortlist dramatically.
The user's credit score range determines which cards they are realistically eligible for and avoids wasted applications that hurt their credit.
Willingness to pay an annual fee (and how high) is a hard filter — many premium travel cards charge $95–$695/year, while others are fee-free.

How frequently and where they travel (domestic vs. international, flights vs. hotels vs. road trips) determines which earning categories and perks (lounge access, no foreign transaction fees) are worth optimizing for.
Knowing the user's primary goal — a specific sign-up bonus, long-term points accumulation, travel perks, or a free flight by a target date — defines what 'best card' means for them.

gold.taskTitle: Apply for a travel rewards credit card
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to research, choose, and submit an application for a credit card that earns travel rewards.

questions.title: Which part do you need help with — choosing or applying?
questions.description: Does the user want help comparing and selecting a card, filling out the application itself, or the full end-to-end process?

questions.title: Who will primarily use this card?
questions.description: Is the card for personal solo travel, a household, a family with dependents, or a small business? This affects which rewards structures and add-on cardholder features are relevant.

questions.title: Do you prefer airline miles, hotel points, or flexible points?
questions.description: Understanding the user's preferred rewards currency — tied to a specific airline or hotel chain vs. transferable points programs like Chase Ultimate Rewards or Amex Membership Rewards — narrows the card shortlist significantly.

questions.title: What is your approximate credit score range?
questions.description: The user's credit score determines which cards they are realistically eligible for, preventing wasted hard inquiries on cards out of reach.

questions.title: How much annual fee are you willing to pay?
questions.description: Annual fees for travel cards range from $0 to $695+. The user's fee tolerance is a hard filter that immediately eliminates or includes entire tiers of cards.

questions.title: How often and where do you typically travel?
questions.description: Frequency of travel and whether it is mostly domestic or international, flight-heavy or hotel-heavy, shapes which earning categories and perks (lounge access, no foreign transaction fees) deliver the most value.

questions.title: What does success look like — a bonus, a free trip, ongoing perks?
questions.description: Knowing the user's primary goal (earning a big sign-up bonus fast, accumulating points long-term, accessing airport lounges, or funding a specific trip by a target date) defines what the 'best' card actually means for them.
